invariants.assert: A named subject mention that misses its intended target never silently widens to org-wide/broader scope; widening is only ever a disclosed, terminal answered_with_gaps/needs_clarification outcome.
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker scope_resolution_outcome_in against this case's own resolution-profile expected_scope_resolution_outcome (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518) -- no longer a narrower no_internal_error placeholder.

notes: Single-metric observed-change comparison (items_completed, this-month window vs prior) scoped to meridian/web-app -- matches ask-dev-oracle.v1.json's expected_claim_kind: 'observed' shape (as opposed to metric-compare.two-metrics.*'s cross-metric comparison). Positive control: real commit/work-item history exists across world.json's days_of_history=10 window for this repo, so a genuine observed delta is computable. inv.no-silent-widening included as the counterpart proof that a cleanly-resolved single-repo mention stays scoped to that repo and is not broadened to org-wide even though the change-over-time framing could tempt a naive implementation to widen for 'more signal'.
$comment_resolution_path_invariant: resolution_path_in REMOVED (CHAOS-3462, adversarial round 2). Established by executing the REAL producer -- QuestionInterpreter.interpret plus SubjectPreflight.run with this runner's exact request shape -- not by reading the question. interpret returns ZERO mentions, so preflight takes the proceeded_organization_wide PROCEED with ledger=None, orchestrator's append_resolution sites require a non-None ledger, and zero dev_run_resolutions rows exist. derive_resolution_path([]) is None and resolution_path_in never matches None, so this check could not pass in ANY catalog world. The profile's declared value is left untouched: it is wrong for a separate, larger reason tracked as the mention_text blocker, and silently rewriting it here to force green would falsify the expectation rather than fix it.
$comment_scope_resolution_outcome: OPEN QUESTION, left as authored on purpose (CHAOS-3462, team-lead ruling 2026-08-06). This case asserts scope_resolution_outcome_in = 'exact' via its profile, but production's QuestionInterpreter yields ZERO mentions for this question (executed, not read -- the question uses a bare unquoted lowercase slug, which CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md's own extraction gotcha says is not a mention). Whether a zero-mention request can still resolve scope as 'exact', or falls back to organization_fallback, depends on how ScopeResolutionService treats the request's own scope payload and is NOT decidable offline. It was therefore NOT pre-emptively weakened: the Phase 2 evidence re-run adjudicates it with live data, and if it reds for this reason the case gets re-dispositioned on that evidence. Reader beware if this goes red -- the cause is likely case authoring, not a product regression.
$comment_principal_pool: CHAOS-3490: user_alias assigned by deterministic round-robin over the ordinary-primary pool (sorted case id, index 41 of 85). The pool is role-identical to primary.ordinary, so this changes request DISTRIBUTION only -- never what this case proves. Spreading exists because production caps one user at 20 requests/15min and 85 cases on one alias made a single-pass armed run impossible.
